What We Do

Full-Service Urology Revenue Cycle Management

Urology billing combines endoscopic procedure coding, urodynamics testing, stone management procedures, prostate treatment billing, and robotic surgical coding. PMEX reviews every procedure report before coding and manages the full claim lifecycle from submission to payment.

Cystoscopy Billing

Diagnostic and therapeutic cystoscopy codes (52000 to 52355) coded by procedure performed.

Urodynamics Testing

Urodynamics studies (51725 to 51798) billed per the tests performed and documented.

Stone Management

ESWL (50590), ureteroscopy with lithotripsy (52356), and stent codes billed per report.

Prostate Procedure Coding

TURP, laser ablation, and prostate biopsy codes selected from the operative report.

Robotic Surgery Coding

Robotic-assisted urologic procedures billed with correct robotic add-on codes.

PSA and Lab Coordination

PSA and urinary lab codes billed separately from the office visit where applicable.

Sound Familiar?

Common Urology Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Cystoscopy with biopsy billed at diagnostic cystoscopy level, losing the therapeutic code rate.

PMEX reads every cystoscopy report and codes the therapeutic procedure when biopsy, fulguration, or stent placement is documented.

Lithotripsy and ureteral stent billed without confirming both procedures are separately coded.

PMEX reviews ureteroscopy reports for all procedures performed and submits separate codes for lithotripsy and stent placement when both are documented.

Urodynamics components not individually billed, losing revenue on multi-test sessions.

PMEX identifies each urodynamics study from the report and bills every separately payable component.

Robotic prostatectomy submitted without the robotic add-on code alongside the primary CPT.

PMEX applies the robotic surgery add-on (S2900) alongside the primary urologic CPT when robotic technique is documented.

Prior authorization not obtained before elective robotic urologic surgery.

PMEX manages surgical prior authorization with clinical documentation before the OR date is confirmed.

PSA lab code not billed separately from the office visit on the same date of service.

PMEX confirms PSA and other lab codes are submitted separately from the E/M on every visit where lab is ordered and resulted.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Urology Billing

Urology practices lose 15 to 26 percent of revenue to cystoscopy under-coding, stone procedure bundling errors, and robotic surgery authorization gaps.

PATTERN 01

Cystoscopy Under-Coded, Therapeutic Procedure Not Captured

Cystoscopy with bladder tumor fulguration performed (52214, $680). Billing team submits diagnostic cystoscopy (52000, $180). Therapeutic procedure not coded from the operative report. $500 per case under-coded from one code selection error.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reads every cystoscopy operative report and codes the highest-complexity procedure performed: diagnostic, with biopsy, with fulguration, with tumor resection, or with stent placement. Diagnostic codes are applied only when no therapeutic intervention is documented.

PATTERN 02

Ureteral Stent Not Billed Alongside Ureteroscopy

Ureteroscopy with laser lithotripsy performed. 52356 (ureteroscopy with lithotripsy) submitted. Ureteral stent placement (52332) not billed, assumed bundled. Per CCI, 52332 is separately billable alongside 52356 with modifier 51. $180 per case in stent revenue not captured.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews every ureteroscopy report for stent placement documentation and submits 52332 alongside 52356 with modifier 51 when stent placement is separately documented in the operative report.

PATTERN 03

Robotic Prostatectomy Denied, Authorization Not Confirmed

Robotic-assisted laparoscopic prostatectomy scheduled. Commercial payer requires prior authorization for robotic surgical procedures. Case proceeds without confirmed auth. $4,200 professional fee denied. Retroactive authorization not available.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX manages surgical prior authorization for all robotic urologic procedures, confirming authorization is in the billing system before the OR date is placed on the schedule, with clinical documentation of diagnosis and procedure indication attached.

Urology Billing Questions Answered

Yes. 52332 (ureteral stent placement) is separately billable alongside 52356 (ureteroscopy with lithotripsy) with modifier 51 when both are documented in the operative report.

Each urodynamics component (uroflowmetry, cystometrogram, pressure flow study, EMG) is billed separately with its own CPT code. We identify each test from the urodynamics report and bill every separately payable component.

Yes. Robotic-assisted urologic procedures use the primary open or laparoscopic CPT code alongside the robotic add-on code. We confirm the robotic technique from the operative report before applying the add-on.

We obtain prior authorization before the OR date is confirmed for all elective urologic procedures, with clinical documentation of diagnosis, prior treatment, and procedure indication submitted to the payer.
